Create a 3D annotation specification

Source: R/annotate-3d.R
annotate_3d.Rd

Defines fixed-position annotations to be embedded within a 3D layer. Annotations are depth-sorted together with the primary geometry, unlike ggplot2's annotate() which creates a separate layer.

Usage

annotate_3d(type, ...)

Arguments

type

Character string specifying the annotation type. One of "point", "text", "segment", "polygon", "axes", "line", or "plane".

...

Type-specific parameters. See Details.

Value

An S3 object of class "annotate_3d".

Details

Parameters can be vectors to create multiple annotations of the same type in one call, with scalar values recycled as needed (matching ggplot2::annotate() behaviour).

Point annotations

Requires x, y, z. Optional styling: colour/color, fill, size, shape, alpha, stroke.

Text annotations

Requires x, y, z, label. Optional styling: colour/color, size, alpha, family, fontface, hjust, vjust, angle, lineheight.

By default, labels are depth-sorted with the rest of the layer, so geometry in front of a label hides it. Set on_top = TRUE to draw labels on top of everything else in the layer instead, keeping them legible wherever they fall (e.g. labels in a diagram). on_top can be a vector, to set it per label.

Segment annotations

Requires x, y, z, xend, yend, zend. Optional styling: colour/color, linewidth, linetype, alpha, and arrow, an arrow specification created by grid::arrow() that applies to every segment in the call. Closed arrowheads are filled with the segment colour. When a segment passes through a polygon and is split, its arrowheads stay at the segment's original ends.

Polygon annotations

Requires x, y, z giving the polygon's vertices in order. To draw several polygons in one call, give group, with one value per vertex; vertices sharing a value form one polygon. Each polygon needs at least 3 vertices. Optional styling: fill (default "grey60"), alpha (default 0.5), colour/color for the outline (default "grey30"), linewidth, linetype. Styling values apply per polygon, so they must have length 1 or one value per polygon, in the order the groups first appear.

Like planes, polygons are lit from whichever side faces the viewer and are never removed by back-face culling. Unlike planes, they are placed in data space, so they expand the plot's axis ranges to fit.

Axes annotations

Draws a line along each of the x, y, and z axes through an origin given by x, y, z (default 0), each spanning the panel's full range along its axis, with an arrowhead and a label at its high end. Optional: labels (a length-3 vector, default c("x", "y", "z"), or NULL for none), arrow (default a closed 6pt arrowhead, or NULL for none), line styling colour/color, linewidth, linetype, alpha, and label styling size, family, fontface. Styling values can have length 3 to style each axis separately.

Axes are built from the panel's limits when the plot is drawn, so unlike other annotations they don't expand the plot's axis ranges.

Line annotations

Draws infinite lines, clipped to the panel. Each line passes through the point x, y, z (each defaulting to 0) in the direction dx, dy, dz (each defaulting to 0, but not all zero). For example, the line spanned by a vector v is annotate_3d("line", dx = v[1], dy = v[2], dz = v[3]), and the vertical line at x = 1, y = 2 is annotate_3d("line", x = 1, y = 2, dz = 1). All values can be vectors to draw several lines. Optional styling: colour/color, linewidth, linetype, alpha.

Like axes and planes, lines are built from the panel's limits and don't expand the plot's axis ranges. A line that misses the panel entirely is skipped with a warning.

Plane annotations

Draws planes, clipped to the panel. Each call gives its planes in one of three forms:

  • xintercept, yintercept, or zintercept: planes perpendicular to an axis, e.g. yintercept = 2 for the plane y = 2. Only one of the three can be used per call.

  • intercept, slope_x, slope_y: the plane z = intercept + slope_x * x + slope_y * y, as from a linear model. Any of the three left out defaults to 0.

  • a, b, c, d: the general form a * x + b * y + c * z = d. Requires a, b, c (not all zero); d defaults to 0.

Values can be vectors to draw several planes. In the general form, for example, a, b, c can be the columns of a matrix A and d the right-hand side of the linear system A x = d. To combine forms, use separate annotate_3d() calls. Optional styling: fill (default "grey60"), alpha (default 0.5), colour/color for the outline (default none), linewidth, linetype.

Like axes, planes are built from the panel's limits and don't expand the plot's axis ranges. They are lit like the layer's other polygons, from whichever side faces the viewer, and are never removed by back-face culling. A plane that misses the panel entirely is skipped with a warning.

Planes are split where they intersect each other or other polygons, and hide the elements they pass in front of (see sorting_methods).

Coordinates

Annotation coordinates are placed directly in the plot's (transformed) scale space: with scale_x_log10(), for example, give x positions as log10 values.

Coincident elements

A point, segment, line, or text label lying exactly in the plane of a polygon (such as a line drawn along a plane, or along the intersection of two planes) is drawn on top of that polygon.

Examples

p <- ggplot(mountain, aes(x, y, z)) +
  coord_3d(ratio = c(2, 3, 1),
           light = light(mode = "hsl", direction = c(-1, 0, 0)))

# Basic point annotation
p + geom_surface_3d(
  annotate = annotate_3d("point", x = .5, y = .25, z = 100,
                         color = "red", size = 3))


# Vectorized: multiple points in one call
p + geom_surface_3d(
  annotate = annotate_3d("point", x = .5, y = .25, z = seq(50, 100, 5),
                         color = "red", size = 3))


# Multiple annotation types
p + geom_surface_3d(
  annotate = list(
    annotate_3d("point", x = .5, y = .25, z = 100,
                color = "red", size = 3),
    annotate_3d("text", x = .5, y = .25, z = 100,
                color = "red", label = "Look here!",
                vjust = -1, fontface = "bold"),
    annotate_3d("segment", x = .5, y = .25, z = 100,
                xend = .5, yend = .25, zend = 50,
                color = "red", size = 3)))


# Planes of a linear system, meeting at its solution, and the line along
# which the first two planes intersect
A <- rbind(c(1, 1, 1), c(1, -1, 0), c(0, 1, -1))
ggplot(data.frame(x = 1/3, y = 1/3, z = 1/3), aes(x, y, z)) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 3,
                annotate = list(
                  annotate_3d("plane", a = A[, 1], b = A[, 2],
                              c = A[, 3], d = c(1, 0, 0),
                              fill = c("tomato", "seagreen", "steelblue")),
                  annotate_3d("line", x = 1/3, y = 1/3, z = 1/3,
                              dx = 1, dy = 1, dz = -2, linewidth = 1))) +
  lims(x = c(-1, 1), y = c(-1, 1)) + zlim(-1, 1) +
  coord_3d()


# A fitted regression plane, with a horizontal reference plane
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
b <- coef(fit)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, hp, mpg)) +
  geom_point_3d(annotate = list(
    annotate_3d("plane", intercept = b[1], slope_x = b["wt"], slope_y = b["hp"],
                fill = "steelblue"),
    annotate_3d("plane", zintercept = 20, alpha = 0.3))) +
  coord_3d(yaw = 120)


# A polygon: the triangle spanned by two vectors and the origin
u <- c(1, 0.2, 0.5); v <- c(0.3, 1, 0.8)
ggplot(data.frame(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, xend = c(u[1], v[1]),
                  yend = c(u[2], v[2]), zend = c(u[3], v[3])),
       aes(x, y, z, xend = xend, yend = yend, zend = zend)) +
  geom_segment_3d(arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(8, "pt")),
                  annotate = annotate_3d("polygon", x = c(0, u[1], v[1]),
                                         y = c(0, u[2], v[2]), z = c(0, u[3], v[3]),
                                         fill = "steelblue")) +
  coord_3d()


# Axes through the origin, depth-sorted with a surface
ggplot() +
  geom_function_3d(fun = function(x, y) (x^2 - y^2) / 2,
                   xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1), n = 20,
                   annotate = annotate_3d("axes", linewidth = 0.8)) +
  coord_3d(panels = "none") +
  theme_void()
